Critically, no red-flag omissions are present: biopsy was appropriately performed and interpreted, infection workup appears adequate, and malignancy screening—while ideally including age-/risk-appropriate imaging or bone marrow if hematologic concern arises—is not mandatory in absence of cytopenias, splenomegaly, or abnormal peripheral smear (none reported). CBC and basic labs are implied as “next steps” but not yet confirmed; however, their absence does *not* invalidate the diagnosis, as PG can be diagnosed clinically and histologically even before identifying an underlying association. At Turn 7/10, we are not at maximum turn limit, but the diagnosis is already sufficiently established — further testing serves to identify comorbidities, not to confirm PG itself.

[DECISION] PASS
